stories.title: Irvine Company Signs Nearly 2.5M SF of Office Leases in Q3
stories.excerpt: Irvine Company signed nearly 2.5 million square feet of office leases in the third quarter, led by deals with Taco Bell and medical technology firm Envista and seizing on the overall demand for Orange County, Calif., space compared with its neighbors. The Newport Beach-based private real estate giant completed 182 leases across its national office portfolio from July through September, generating 722,000 square feet of positive net absorption, Commercial Observer can first report. New leases and expansions accounted for more than 1.36 million square feet, while renewals added another 1.06 million square feet. The largest deal was Taco Bell’s 254,000-square-foot lease at Alton HQ in Irvine, marking Orange County’s largest office lease in five years. The fast-food giant plans to relocate its headquarters to the campus in 2028. Envista signed another 117,700-square-foot lease at Irvine Company’s Lakeview Business Center, while transportation technology company Iteris, part of Almaviva Group, committed to 64,000 square feet at Laguna Canyon in Irvine. Other Southern California transactions included a 46,000-square-foot relocation and expansion by Luminys Systems at Bake Technology Park and a 23,000-square-foot renewal by accounting firm Redwitz at Jamboree Center, both in Irvine. “These commitments reflect the value companies continue to place on high-quality workplaces that support their people and their business,” Roger DeWames, president of office properties at Irvine Company, said in a statement. “From Taco Bell’s major lease at Alton HQ to customers renewing and expanding across our portfolio, we’re seeing companies make significant investments in their office space.” Orange County’s office vacancy declined to 12.1 percent in the third quarter from 13.3 percent in the second quarter, while net absorption reached 300,000 square feet, according to CBRE. Average monthly asking rents increased 11 cents to $3 per square foot per month. Mean
bullets: Irvine Co. signed 2.5M SF office leases in Q3; Taco Bell HQ move 254K SF.
Orange County office demand outpacing LA/neighbors; 722K SF net absorption Q3.
Taco Bell HQ relocation to Alton campus in 2028 signals sustained OC employer confidence.
stories.summary: Irvine Company closed nearly 2.5 million square feet of office leases in Q3, including Taco Bell's 254,000-square-foot headquarters relocation to the Alton campus (occupancy in 2028) and Envista's 117,700-square-foot expansion. The portfolio generated 722,000 square feet of positive net absorption across 182 deals. Orange County is outperforming peer markets in the region for office demand.
stories.impact: Major HQ relocations like Taco Bell signal multi-year job creation and in-migration into Orange County, strengthening rental demand for apartments targeting new employee populations. Developers should prioritize multifamily near office clusters (Irvine submarket) ahead of 2028 occupancy; the continued office leasing momentum validates supply fundamentals in OC that support residential development feasibility and rent growth potential.

stories.title: Dwight Capital Lends $42M on North Carolina Apartments Build
stories.excerpt: An investment group led by Cheferkon Partners has sealed $42 million of U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD)-backed debt to develop a North Carolina multifamily property, Commercial Observer has learned. Dwight Capital originated the HUD 221(d)(4) construction loan for the sponsorship’s planned 184-unit One Salem Apartments project in Winston-Salem, N.C., in a deal originated by Brandon Baksh. The nonrecourse debt was structured with a fully amortizing 40-year term designed to give the borrower long-term stability and predictable service payments, according to Dwight. Greg Chew, who co-founded Cheferkon Partners with Raihan Ferdous, said the property has strong multifamily fundamentals with limited supply in the market, as well as a beneficial location around 10 minutes from Downtown Winston-Salem with a number of major retailers nearby, including Walmart and Target. He noted that its close proximity to Wake Forest University is another demand driver. Located at 119 Brookstown Avenue on a 15-acre site four miles south of Wake Forest, the garden-style apartment complex will have units ranging from one to three bedrooms along with detached garages in eight buildings. Community amenities will include a clubhouse, a fitness center, a business center, a swimming pool, barbeque grilling stations, a pickleball court and a dog park. The One Salem Apartments project is slated for full completion in 2028, but Cheferkon hopes to have the first building finished by 2027’s third quarter. Chew noted that the loan’s flexible structure is conducive given that the lease-up of the property will happen in phases. “We have an anticipated lease-up schedule as soon as the buildings start coming online,” Chew said. “That starts to build up income, and that helps offset some of the financing costs.” Ferdous said the investment group for One Salem Apartments has five other partners, and Cheferkon is looking to add more partners by the end of the year. bullets: Dwight Capital closed $42M HUD 221(d)(4) loan for 184-unit One Salem Apartments, Winston-Salem NC.
40-year amortizing nonrecourse structure; limited supply and proximity to downtown/retail anchors cited.
HUD financing availability remains robust for secondary markets with constrained multifamily supply.
stories.summary: Cheferkon Partners secured a $42 million HUD 221(d)(4) construction loan from Dwight Capital for the 184-unit One Salem Apartments in Winston-Salem, North Carolina. The deal features a fully amortizing 40-year nonrecourse structure. The sponsor cited strong fundamentals driven by limited supply, downtown proximity, and nearby retail anchors (Walmart, Target).
stories.impact: HUD lending appetite for secondary markets remains durable, enabling smaller developments where conventional financing may be tight. Winston-Salem's constrained supply (a key underwriting driver here) is typical of Tier 2 metros; developers entering similar markets should model aggressive rent growth and extended hold periods to justify development now, as supply remains structurally limited.

stories.title: DC Multifamily Sales Volume Surpasses 2025 Total
stories.excerpt: The Washington, D.C., multifamily market has shown further signs of stabilization as the pace of new deliveries has slowed, coinciding with easing employment losses, according to a recent report by Northmarq. Investment activity strengthened in the third quarter, with 16 properties trading for $1.8 billion, pushing year-to-date volume above the 2025 total. The year-to-date median sale price is $297,800 per unit. Regional vacancy declined 10 basis points to 5.7%, the first quarterly decline in more than a year, though it remains 60 basis points above one year ago. Asking rents were unchanged from the second quarter but remain down 0.8% year-over-year. Northern Virginia rents were nearly flat from a year ago, and the decline in Class A rents has narrowed. How broad the recovery becomes regionally will depend on the District and Suburban Maryland, where trades include smaller and older assets and where vacancy has eased for two straight quarters, but rents are still falling. The post DC Multifamily Sales Volume Surpasses 2025 Total appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: DC multifamily YTD sales volume $1.8B (16 properties Q3); exceeds full 2025 total.
Median price $297.8K/unit; vacancy down 10 bps to 5.7% (first quarterly decline in 12+ months).
Asking rents flat Q2-Q3, down 0.8% YoY; Northern VA rents near flat YoY.
stories.summary: Washington, D.C.'s multifamily market showed stabilization signs in Q3 as deliveries slowed and employment losses eased. Investment activity strengthened with 16 properties trading for $1.8 billion year-to-date, surpassing the 2025 total. Regional vacancy declined 10 basis points to 5.7%—the first quarterly improvement in over a year—though it remains 60 bps above year-ago levels. Median sale price stands at $297,800 per unit; asking rents are flat sequentially but down 0.8% annually.
stories.impact: DC's first vacancy decline in 12+ months signals supply overhang is absorbing; however, asking rents remain under pressure YoY. Developers should watch delivery pipelines closely—if new supply continues decelerating into 2025, rent growth can re-accelerate. Current investment cap rates (implied by $297.8K pricing) may not fully reflect recovery trajectory; acquisition windows for value-add or lease-up assets are narrowing as confidence returns to the market.

stories.title: Work Begins on 420-Unit Residential Development in Ballston
stories.excerpt: Hoffman & Associates, alongside development partners Snell Properties and Mitsui Fudosan America, Inc. (MFA), today broke ground on 4600 Fairfax, a new residential community in Arlington’s Ballston neighborhood. Spanning more than four acres, the approximately 550,000-square-foot development will deliver 420 residential apartment units and more than 380 parking spaces in a seven-story multifamily building as part of its first phase. Plans also include site preparation for a separate for-sale residential component, with the project designed to achieve LEED Gold certification. Located in the heart of Ballston, 4600 Fairfax offers residents seamless connectivity to Metro, retail and major employment centers in one of Northern Virginia’s most vibrant neighborhoods. The groundbreaking follows the project’s $195 million financing announcement earlier this year. That transaction was brokered by Berkadia and included a senior construction loan from Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group (MUFG). With construction underway, 4600 Fairfax adds to Hoffman & Associates’ active development pipeline across the Mid-Atlantic and Southeast. The post Work Begins on 420-Unit Residential Development in Ballston appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Hoffman & Associates broke ground on 420-unit 4600 Fairfax in Arlington Ballston.
$195M construction financing via MUFG; 550K SF across 7 stories + future for-sale component.
Metro-proximate, high-density Ballston location near employment centers; LEED Gold target.
stories.summary: Hoffman & Associates, Snell Properties, and Mitsui Fudosan America broke ground on 4600 Fairfax, a 420-unit multifamily development in Arlington's Ballston neighborhood. The project spans 550,000 square feet across seven stories with 380+ parking spaces and aims for LEED Gold certification. It was financed with $195 million in construction debt led by MUFG and brokered by Berkadia. The development also includes planning for a separate for-sale residential component.
stories.impact: Northern Virginia continues to attract institutional capital for large-scale multifamily projects backed by transit access and employment proximity. Ballston's density and Metro connectivity make it a premium submarket; cost inflation (visible in $195M+ financing for 420 units) suggests high per-unit development costs. Developers in similar Northern VA submarkets should expect competitive acquisition activity and rising land values as major sponsors queue capital into the region.

stories.title: Eli Lilly Breaks Ground on $3.5B Lehigh Valley Manufacturing Campus
stories.excerpt: Eli Lilly and Company broke ground on a $3.5 billion manufacturing facility in Pennsylvania’s Lehigh Valley. The site is one of 10 new U.S. manufacturing sites announced since 2020, and one of four dedicated to injectable medicines and devices. Part of the company’s $50 billion push to expand medicine production in the U.S., the Lehigh Valley site will add capacity for the next generation of treatments.The new facility will create 850 high-wage jobs along with approximately 2,000 construction jobs as the site is built and brought online. The Lehigh Valley site, located in Fogelsville, Pennsylvania, is expected to be operational by 2031.“Today marks another historic milestone in Pennsylvania’s thriving life sciences sector and reinforces my Administration’s commitment to advancing innovation, strengthening the economy, and creating good-paying jobs across the Commonwealth,” said Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro. Mark Goode to Receive Lifetime Achievement Award at Connect Industrial Midwest on Tuesday, March 2, 2027, at Joe’s Live in Rosemont. Following the presentation, Mark Goode will sit down for a special keynote interview with his son, Matt Goode. The post Eli Lilly Breaks Ground on $3.5B Lehigh Valley Manufacturing Campus appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Eli Lilly broke ground on $3.5B Lehigh Valley PA manufacturing campus in Fogelsville.
850 permanent jobs plus ~2K construction jobs; operational target 2031.
Part of $50B U.S. production expansion; one of four injectable medicines/device sites nationwide.
stories.summary: Eli Lilly broke ground on a $3.5 billion manufacturing facility in Fogelsville, Pennsylvania (Lehigh Valley), creating 850 high-wage permanent jobs and approximately 2,000 construction jobs over build-out. The facility is expected to be operational by 2031 and is one of four U.S. sites dedicated to injectable medicines and devices as part of Eli Lilly's $50 billion domestic production expansion announced since 2020.
stories.impact: Large-scale pharmaceutical manufacturing brings sustained job growth and high wage premiums to the Lehigh Valley, driving multi-year population in-migration and stronger rental demand. Developers should prioritize apartment developments within 15–20 minutes of Fogelsville and within proximity to existing employment centers (Bethlehem Steel corridor); pipeline should be timed for delivery 2028–2031 to capture employee relocation waves. The 2031 operational timeline creates a 5-year window for land acquisition and entitlement in adjacent markets.

stories.title: Ytech Lands $42M Loan for Second Brickell Condo Tower
stories.excerpt: Development firm Ytech has obtained a $42 million pre-development loan from Linkvest Capital for a condo tower in Miami’s Brickell district. Last week, Ytech launched sales for the planned 52-story development called 75 Broadway. The financing from Linkvest Capital’s affiliate LV Lending refinances a $19.5 million pre-development loan from Israel Discount Bank issued in 2024. The high-rise will feature 106 units and 42,000 square feet of amenities. It’s planned for 41 and 75 Southwest 15th Road, near the southern tip of the business district, two blocks west of Brickell Avenue, and across the street from Simpson Rockland Hammock Preserve Park. Prices start at $3 million, with completion slated for late 2029. The developer assembled the 0.3-acre site between 2018 and 2020, paying a combined $8.2 million, according to property records. “The site’s zoning allowed nearly 300 residences. We deliberately chose to build just 106, so we could create residences with generous proportions, exceptional views, superior privacy, and truly personalized service,” Yamal Yidios, founder and CEO of Ytech, said in a statement. 75 Broadway’s financing comes a year after Ytech secured a $565 million construction loan for the nearby 70-story 1428 Brickell luxury condominium tower. In 2024, Linkvest Capital had provided a $78 million pre-development loan for that project. Along the historic portion of Brickell Avenue, Ytech owns two mansions, one leased to Major Food Group’s Chateau ZZ restaurant and another, which the firm is expanding after landing $25 million in financing this year. A representative for Ytech did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Ytech secured $42M pre-dev loan (Linkvest) for 52-story, 106-unit condo tower 75 Broadway, Miami Brickell.
Pricing starts $3M/unit; completion late 2029; refinanced prior $19.5M Israel Discount loan.
Ultra-luxury condo supply tightening in Brickell; intentionally limited unit count for privacy/proportions.
stories.summary: Ytech obtained a $42 million pre-development loan from Linkvest Capital for the 52-story 75 Broadway condo tower in Miami's Brickell district. The development features 106 units and 42,000 square feet of amenities, with pricing starting at $3 million per unit and completion targeted for late 2029. Ytech assembled the 0.3-acre site between 2018 and 2020 for $8.2 million combined; it deliberately limited density (site could support ~300 units) to maximize unit quality.
stories.impact: Ultra-luxury condo development in Brickell remains well-capitalized despite rate environment; financing availability for pre-development signals continued investor appetite for high-price-point residential. However, this is condo-specific and limited relevance to multifamily rental development. Rental developers in Brickell should note limited ground opportunities and premium land costs ($27M+ per acre implied); focus strategy on less-constrained nearby submarkets or conversion opportunities rather than new ground-up rental construction.

stories.title: Developers Propose New Site for $10B Chicago Bears Stadium
stories.excerpt: Developers have unveiled a $10 billion proposal for a large-scale development district in Bronzeville that would include a domed Chicago Bears stadium and thousands of new residential units. The proposal, led by Capri Investment Group and Grit Chicago, would span about 100 acres, extending from the former Michael Reese Hospital site to Prairie Shores and above the McCormick Place marshaling yard. Plans call for a domed stadium with a capacity of about 75,000 people. Capri and its partners offered to buy the Bears’ Arlington Heights property if owning that land is a barrier to the team committing to a Chicago site. The development would include more than 5,000 new homes, including at least 1,000 units designated as affordable and senior housing. The latest Bronzeville proposal is the second stadium plan put forth by developers. The other proposed location is the former U.S. Steel site on the city’s Southeast Side. The post Developers Propose New Site for $10B Chicago Bears Stadium appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Capri/Grit Chicago propose $10B mixed-use project in Bronzeville: domed Bears stadium + 5K+ homes.
5,000+ units including 1K+ affordable/senior; 100 acres from Michael Reese site to McCormick marshaling yard.
Proposal includes 75K-seat stadium; developers offer to purchase Bears Arlington Heights property if needed.
stories.summary: Capri Investment Group and Grit Chicago unveiled a $10 billion mixed-use proposal spanning ~100 acres in Chicago's Bronzeville, including a domed 75,000-seat Bears stadium and 5,000+ new residential units (with minimum 1,000 affordable/senior units). The development would extend from the former Michael Reese Hospital site to Prairie Shores and above the McCormick Place marshaling yard. This is the second stadium proposal; the other targets the former U.S. Steel Southeast Side site.
stories.impact: Large-scale mixed-use/stadium projects face entitlement risk and long timelines; neither Bronzeville nor Southeast Side site has been approved. If either moves forward, it will unlock massive land value and multi-phase residential development. Developers should monitor zoning/TIF eligibility and infrastructure plans—successful approval could unlock 5–10 year pipeline of Build-to-Rent and mixed-income opportunities in currently under-resourced South Side submarkets. However, execution and financing certainty remain low until municipal/NFL agreement solidifies.

stories.title: MD Squared Property Group Takes 16K SF at Feil’s 145 West 30th Street
stories.excerpt: MD Squared Property Group, a New York City-based property management firm, has signed a 16,376-square-foot lease at the Feil Organization’s 145 West 30th Street in Midtown South, Commercial Observer has learned. The deal brings the 12-story office building to 100 percent occupancy. “Reaching 100 percent capacity is an important milestone and reflects the continued demand we’re seeing for well-located, full-floor office space,” Andrew Wiener, head of commercial leasing at Feil, said in a statement. “MD Squared’s commitment to two full floors builds on the building’s recent leasing momentum and reflects a tightening market where tenants continue to prioritize quality space, efficient floor plates and convenient transit access.” Wiener represented Feil in-house on this deal, while the tenant represented itself. MD Squared will occupy the entire third and fourth floors of 145 West 30th Street, relocating from 7 Pennsylvania Plaza, Feil told CO. The length of the lease and the asking rent were not disclosed. The average asking rent for office space in Midtown Manhattan was $85.08 per square foot during the third quarter of 2026, according to data from Colliers. “We’re excited to partner with the Feil Organization, whose long-standing commitment to supporting our communities reflects priorities that are equally important to MD Squared,” Michael Mintz, CEO and founder of MD Squared, said in a statement. “Those shared values, together with the strong relationship we’ve built, made 145 West 30th Street a natural fit for our team.” Built in 1913, 145 West 30th Street is a 12-story office building near the Penn District, Madison Square Garden and Pennsylvania Station. Other tenants in the building include continuing education provider the Tuner School, as well as Wave Sports and Entertainment. Amanda Schiavo can be reached at aschiavo@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: MD Squared Property Group leased 16.4K SF at Feil's 145 West 30th Street, Midtown South Manhattan.
Building reached 100% occupancy; tenant relocating from 7 Pennsylvania Plaza (full floors 3-4).
Strong demand for full-floor, efficient office space near transit in Manhattan submarkets.
stories.summary: MD Squared Property Group, a New York City property management firm, signed a 16,376-square-foot lease at Feil Organization's 145 West 30th Street in Midtown South, bringing the 12-story office building to full occupancy. MD Squared will occupy entire floors 3 and 4, relocating from 7 Pennsylvania Plaza. Feil highlighted tenant demand for quality, full-floor office with efficient layouts and transit proximity.
stories.impact: Minimal relevance to multifamily development. This reflects office market conditions (tightening availability, transit-proximate premium) but does not signal demand drivers for rental apartments. Note: If office recovery persists in Midtown South, employee retention and corporate relocations from elsewhere could modestly support nearby multifamily (e.g., Hudson Yards, Chelsea), but the signal is indirect and secondary.

stories.title: Dallas Okays Zoning for Massive Mixed-Use Project
stories.excerpt: Burk Interests and Greenway Investment Co. have been greenlit by the Dallas City Council to build an $800 million mixed-use project. The 9-6 vote was illustrative of the uphill battle the developers faced during the process. The vote came after the height requirements were reduced from 325 to 199 feet, effectively allowing a 17-story building. The development would include three towers: a hospitality tower with 150 hotel keys and 54 condominium units, a 200,000-square-foot office building, and a 177-unit multifamily high-rise. The site at Preston Road and Royal Lane has been vacant since 2019, when it was demolished by a tornado. Developers must fund local infrastructure upgrades, including new traffic signal equipment at Preston and Royal, an emergency vehicle traffic signal for Dallas Fire-Rescue Station 41, and local water/sewage improvements. The post Dallas Okays Zoning for Massive Mixed-Use Project appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Dallas City Council approved $800M mixed-use project (Burk/Greenway) on Preston/Royal after 9-6 vote.
Height reduced 325→199 ft (17-story max); 177 units MF + 150 hotel + 200K SF office.
Developer funds infrastructure; site vacant since 2019 tornado demolition.
stories.summary: Dallas City Council approved an $800 million mixed-use development by Burk Interests and Greenway Investment Co. on Preston Road at Royal Lane in a 9-6 vote. Height restrictions were reduced from 325 to 199 feet (17-story maximum). The project includes a 177-unit multifamily high-rise, 150-key hotel tower, 54 condos, and a 200,000-square-foot office component. Developers must fund local infrastructure improvements (traffic signals, water/sewage). The site has been vacant since a 2019 tornado demolition.
stories.impact: Hard-fought zoning approval (9-6 vote suggests neighborhood resistance) signals Dallas is tightening density/entitlement in some submarkets. Reduced height and infrastructure cost-sharing increase per-unit development costs for the MF component; at 177 units, soft costs and carries are elevated. Developers in Preston-Royal or similar contested submarkets should model longer entitlement timelines and higher infrastructure mitigation costs; focus capital on pre-approved or less-scrutinized Dallas locations with faster paths to construction and lower carry risk.

stories.title: Child Center of NY Signs 16K-SF Lease in New Astoria Office Development
stories.excerpt: A children’s counseling center is opening another location in Queens after signing a lease in Astoria. The Child Center of NY, a nonprofit that provides children with life skills and behavioral health guidance, has signed a 16,082-square-foot lease at Stellar Management’s 35-01 36th Avenue. The Astoria location will be added to Child Center’s roster of over 70 locations, according to landlord broker NY Space Finders. The lease term is for 10 years and the asking rent for the space was $50 per square foot. Luca DiCiero and Faisal Gilani of NY Space Finders represented the landlord in the transaction while Gail Roseman of Sholom & Zuckerbrot negotiated on behalf of the tenant. Roseman did not immediately respond to a request for comment. News of the deal was first posted on social media platform Traded earlier this week with a closing date of Oct. 27. The Astoria property is a nine-story mixed-use development completed in 2024 by Stellar and designed by NDKazalas Architecture, according to New York YIMBY. Other office tenants at 35-01 36th Avenue include coworking firm International Workplace Group, which signed on as its anchor tenant with 8,041 square feet in January 2025. Founded in Queens in 1953, the Child Center of New York is a large operation with over 1,000 employees working in underserved neighborhoods across New York City and Long Island. Its administrative office is at 118-35 Queens Boulevard in Forest Hills, Queens. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Child Center of NY signed 16.1K SF at Stellar's 35-01 36th Ave, Astoria Queens (10-year lease).
Asking rent $50/SF; 9-story mixed-use building completed 2024; nonprofit tenant expansion.
New office supply in Queens; institutional/nonprofit anchor tenants attracting secondary investment.
stories.summary: The Child Center of New York, a nonprofit providing behavioral health services, leased 16,082 square feet at Stellar Management's 35-01 36th Avenue in Astoria for a 10-year term at $50 per square foot. This is part of Child Center's 70+ location network. The building is a newly completed (2024) nine-story mixed-use development.
stories.impact: Minimal direct relevance to multifamily development. Office/institutional leasing in Queens reflects some demand for secondary market space, but does not signal multifamily supply constraints or rental demand drivers. However, note: sustained office/nonprofit institutional activity in Astoria validates long-term demand for mixed-use development; developers with multifamily/office packages in outer-borough Queens locations should proceed with confidence in mixed-use feasibility and long-term stabilization.

stories.title: Broe Group Makes 1st Dallas Acquisition
stories.excerpt: Maple Terrace Residences in Uptown Dallas. Image courtesy of Broe Real Estate Broe Real Estate Group, the real estate arm of the Broe Group, has acquired Maple Terrace Residences in Dallas, a 22-story, 345-unit apartment community in the Uptown district of the city. The seller was a joint venture between Hines, McNair Interests, Mitsui Fudosan America. Broe has rail and real estate holdings in Texas, but this deal marks its entry into the Dallas multifamily market. The parties involved did not disclose the price, though they did say that it was an all-cash deal. The Dallas Business Journal reported that the Dallas Central Appraisal District most recently valued the entirety of the mixed-use Maple Terrace at more than $250 million, but that figure also covers the office and retail portions of the development not acquired by Broe. JLL Capital Markets Investment Sales and Advisory Teams represented the seller in the transaction. Hines will continue to manage the property. Maple Terrace Residences, located at 3003 Maple Ave., opened in 2024 and is part of the new mixed-use Maple Terrace development. The property offers one-, two-, three- and four-bedroom residences and is nearly 92 percent occupied, according to Yardi Matrix. LISTEN HERE: Top Marketers: Multifamily Marketing Strategies From Master-Planned Communities Common-area amenities include a fitness center, a media room, a club house, a swimming pool and a business center. All units include washers and dryers, microwaves and digital locks; some units include fireplaces. There are 811 parking spaces within the structure. About $180.6 million in permanent financing, originated by Sumitomo Mitsui Bank in 2021, is associated with the property, Yardi Matrix reports. bullets: Broe Real Estate acquired Maple Terrace Residences, Dallas Uptown: 345-unit, 22-story, all-cash deal.
Property opened 2024; 92% occupied; seller was Hines/McNair/Mitsui JV; Hines continues mgmt.
Broe's first Dallas multifamily acquisition; entry into Uptown rental market with stabilized asset.
stories.summary: Broe Real Estate Group, the real estate arm of Broe Group, acquired Maple Terrace Residences in Dallas's Uptown district—a 345-unit, 22-story apartment community that opened in 2024. The all-cash purchase (price not disclosed; property valued ~$250M+) marks Broe's entry into Dallas multifamily. The property is 92% occupied with $180.6 million in permanent financing from Sumitomo Mitsui Bank (2021 origination). Hines continues property management. The seller was a JV of Hines, McNair Interests, and Mitsui Fudosan America.
stories.impact: Broe's all-cash acquisition of a brand-new, stabilized Uptown property signals capital is flowing to well-located, recently delivered assets in Dallas. This sets a high bar for acquisition pricing and limits ground-up development urgency in Uptown near-term. However, Broe's entry (with $8B AUM) may accelerate competitive positioning; developers should focus on pre-lease/construction-ready projects in secondary Dallas submarkets or alternative product types (55+, student, workforce) where competition is less acute and yield requirements are less compressed.

stories.title: Top Marketers: Multifamily Marketing Strategies From Master-Planned Communities
stories.excerpt: Multifamily marketing used to focus on what sat inside the four walls: the kitchens, the fixtures, the views. Today it’s about lifestyle, community and the experience a brand delivers long after move-in day. The strongest multifamily marketing strategies help shape places, not just promote them. This episode of Multi-Housing News’ Top Marketers podcast explores how multifamily marketing strategies can guide development, positioning and the resident experience in multifamily, master-planned and mixed-use communities. Joining us are Carly Catalana and Kevin Wilson, senior vice presidents and co-heads of marketing at Southern Land Company. Together they lead marketing strategy across a national portfolio of multifamily, mixed-use and master-planned communities. Catalana started out in luxury fashion and Class A shopping centers, and her focus is branding, placemaking and activations. Wilson spent years at Toll Brothers, Home Properties and Kushner, and he brings deep experience in research, consumer insights and performance. The two call themselves “yin and yang.” They explain how sharing the top marketing role works and how Southern Land’s vertically integrated, hold-to-own model gives marketing a seat at the table from day one. That ranges from choosing amenities for a 55-plus community to adding infrared saunas as wellness becomes a top request from residents. The conversation covers why ‘the community will tell you what it is,’ how storytelling and data work together to fill hard-to-lease units, and what multifamily marketing strategies can learn from master-planned development. Key topics include building a cohesive brand across apartments, for-sale homes and hospitality, avoiding cookie-cutter development, nurturing prospects over several years, attribution problems in a world with many touchpoints and what multifamily can learn from master-planned marketing. From Fashion and Hospitality to Real Estate (0:53) Marketing Pl
bullets: Southern Land Co. co-heads discuss marketing strategy shift: lifestyle/community over unit features.
Vertically integrated, hold-to-own model embeds marketing in site selection and amenity decisions.
Podcast explores placemaking, wellness trends, branding across multifamily/mixed-use/master-planned communities.
stories.summary: Multi-Housing News podcast features Carly Catalana and Kevin Wilson, co-heads of marketing at Southern Land Company. They discuss how multifamily marketing strategy has evolved from focusing on unit interiors to emphasizing lifestyle, community experience, and placemaking. Southern Land's vertically integrated, hold-to-own model gives marketing influence from site selection through amenity planning (e.g., adding infrared saunas as wellness demand rises). The conversation covers branding consistency, storytelling, data-driven leasing, and lessons from master-planned development.
stories.impact: Minimal direct market impact; this is an industry commentary/best-practice piece. However, it reflects a broader trend: premium positioning and amenity differentiation are becoming more critical to stabilization and NOI in competitive markets. Developers should ensure marketing/leasing expertise is engaged at site selection and pro forma stages (not post-construction); wellness, community gathering, and experiential amenities will increasingly drive unit absorption and rent premiums, especially in saturated markets.

stories.title: Exclusive: Rainbow Housing Pays $42M for LA Senior Community
stories.excerpt: Norwalk Tower Apartments opened in 1974 and underwent a $12 million redevelopment in 2014. Image courtesy of Yardi Matrix Rainbow Housing has purchased Norwalk Tower Apartments, an 185-unit affordable and age-restricted community in Norwalk, Calif., according to Yardi Matrix information. Preservation Partners sold the asset for $41.9 million or $226.678 per unit. Rainbow financed the acquisition with an undisclosed amount drawn from a $145.3 million Fannie Mae line of credit originated by Jones Lang LaSalle and maturing in 2041. Developers eyeing affordable senior communities should recognize limited exit pathways (LIHTC/Section 8 restrictions extend holding periods) but benefit from stable, long-term NOI and favorable financing. Geographic focus: Los Angeles County affordable seniors are premium assets given income levels and scarcity; development economics favor smaller communities and adaptive reuse over new ground-up.

stories.title: Advanced Real Estate Pays $56M for Inland Empire Asset
stories.excerpt: Casitas Apartment Homes underwent renovations in 2020. Image courtesy of The Mogharebi Group Advanced Real Estate has acquired the 253-unit Casitas Apartment Homes in Ontario, Calif., for $56.2 million. The Mogharebi Group represented the seller, which Yardi Matrix data identified as Benedict Canyon Equities. Advanced also assumed the property’s existing debt. The Freddie Mac $33.2 million loan, originated by Optigo lender KeyBank in 2020, carries an interest rate of 3.11 percent and is due in 2030, the same data provider shows. The Casitas acquisition closed through Advanced’s X Fund, which operates by purchasing stakes in assets across Southern California and subsequently engaging in 1031 tax-deferred exchanges of the smaller properties into larger communities. Equity from 13 smaller properties was used to buy Casitas, according to prepared remarks by Advanced Real Estate President Paul Julian. Amenities at the property, which also features 27 affordable units, consist of a playground and picnic and barbecue areas. Located on nearly 15 acres at 1900 S. Campus Ave., Casitas is more than 1 mile from the interchange between U.S. routes 60 and 83. A large industrial employment center is just across the street, serving the nearby Ontario International Airport where companies such as Amazon, FedEx and UPS operate. The deal assumed the existing $33.2 million Freddie Mac loan (3.11% fixed rate, due 2030, originated 2020 by KeyBank). stories.impact: Inland Empire multifamily remains attractively priced for value-add and portfolio rollups; low debt assumption (3.11% fixed) suggests refinance at current rates would be challenged, making assume-debt structures more common. Advanced's 1031 aggregation strategy signals capital is consolidating fragmented smaller assets into institutional-quality properties. Developers should note: Inland Empire's affordability and industrial proximity remain structural supports for rental demand; new supply competition is moderate, and employment is durable. Focus development on Class B/C renovation and workforce housing near major logistics corridors (Ontario, Fontana) rather than Class A new construction.

stories.title: Inland JV to Kick Off Minnesota Project
stories.excerpt: The 13-story Citywalk Apartments will come online in 2028. Rendering courtesy of Inland Group Inland National Development Co. and Reuter Walton Development are working on Citywalk Apartments, a 342-unit multifamily project in Rochester, Minn. The community is expected to serve Mayo Clinic’s personnel. The project was initially put forward as a seven-story, 131-unit apartment building. Rochester Economic Development Co. provided $90 million in financing for the project this March, according to Yardi Matrix. ESG Architecture serves as the architect and interior designer. Citywalk is located at 201 6th Ave. SW, in downtown Rochester, close to Mayo Clinic’s and Saint Marys’ downtown campuses. The property will have easy access to Rochester’s pedestrian subway and skyway system and will access the future Link Bus Rapid Transit line. READ ALSO: Top 10 Markets for Multifamily Deliveries The 13-story building is set to come online in 2028 and will feature studio, one-, two- and three-bedroom units, as well as 90 short-term stay apartments. Amenities will feature a rooftop sky terrace, a pool, a year-round sauna, a fitness center, a coworking space, a golf simulator and a game lounge, as well as 250 climate-controlled underground parking spaces. Inland’s total portfolio comprises $16 billion in assets under management. The company developed more than 5 million square feet of multifamily, hospitality, health care, retail, mixed-use and industrial properties across a total of 10,900 acres, including around 7,000 apartment and condominium units and north of 6,000 residential lots. stories.summary: Inland National Development Co. and Reuter Walton Development are building Citywalk Apartments, a 342-unit multifamily project in downtown Rochester, Minnesota. The project was upscaled from an initial 131-unit seven-story concept to 13 stories. Rochester Economic Development Co. provided $90 million in financing in March 2024. The property, scheduled for 2028 delivery, will feature studio through three-bedroom units plus 90 short-term stay apartments, targeting Mayo Clinic personnel. It includes a rooftop sky terrace, pool, sauna, fitness center, coworking, golf simulator, and 250 underground parking spaces.
stories.impact: Mayo Clinic's sustained expansion and workforce demand underpin rental growth and stabilization in Rochester. Developers should recognize: Rochester is a specialized market with outsized dependence on Mayo Clinic employment stability. Citywalk's short-term stay component (90 units) and downtown/transit positioning reflect build-to-suit amenity/workforce housing demand specific to Clinic verticals (medical, research). Non-Clinic-proximate developments in Rochester face higher leasing risk. Consider Mayo Clinic as a fundamental anchor for new multifamily pipeline and source of corporate housing guarantees and relocation demand pre-opening.

stories.title: Bonaventure Buys Hampton Roads Asset for $27M
stories.excerpt: Colonial Towne comprises two-story buildings. Image courtesy of Bonaventure Bonaventure Multifamily Income Trust, a REIT managed by Bonaventure, has acquired Colonial Towne, a 148-unit, garden-style community in Williamsburg, Va. A private individual sold the asset for $27 million, according to Yardi Matrix information. Bellwether Enterprise Real Estate Capital originated a $17.6 million Fannie Mae note carrying a 5.45 percent interest rate. The loan will mature in 2031. Colonial Towne marked the second replacement property in a 1031 exchange that began with the sale of Promenade Pointe, an 183-unit community in Norfolk, Va. The first was the 208-unit Royal Pointe Apartments in Virginia Beach, Va., which Bonaventure acquired in April. Bonaventure now owns 524 units across three Williamsburg communities, including the 228-unit Attain at Quarterpath and the 68-unit Parkway Apartments. The firm’s portfolio comprises 46 properties totaling 9,192 apartments across the Mid-Atlantic and Southeast, according to its website. READ ALSO: Bonaventure CFO on Why Multifamily Distress Remains Contained—for Now Colonial Towne is at 327 Merrimac Trail, near Parkway Apartments and roughly 3 miles from Attain at Quarterpath. Located less than 3 miles from downtown Williamsburg, the property is close to several employers such as Colonial Williamsburg, William & Mary and Busch Gardens. Interstate 64 and Colonial Parkway are also nearby. Completed in 1970, the asset consists of two-story buildings with townhome units and apartments. The unit mix features one-, two- and three-bedroom floorplans averaging 949 square feet. Amenities at the pet-friendly community incorporate a swimming pool, on-site playground and laundry facilities. stories.summary: Bonaventure Multifamily Income Trust (REIT managed by Bonaventure) acquired Colonial Towne, a 148-unit garden-style community in Williamsburg, Virginia, for $27 million. The property was financed with a $17.6 million Fannie Mae loan at 5.45% (due 2031). This acquisition is the second leg of a 1031 exchange initiated by the sale of Promenade Pointe (183 units, Norfolk); the first replacement was Royal Pointe Apartments (208 units, Virginia Beach) acquired in April. Bonaventure now owns 524 units across three Williamsburg properties and maintains a 46-property, 9,192-unit portfolio across the Mid-Atlantic and Southeast.
stories.impact: Bonaventure's active 1031 exchange activity and Williamsburg clustering signal confidence in Hampton Roads rental fundamentals (low supply, stable employment near Colonial Williamsburg, William & Mary, Busch Gardens). 1031 exchanges (especially multi-leg) compress tax drag and allow REIT redeployment into lower-basis assets; investors should monitor cap rates at replacement acquisition—if Bonaventure continues acquiring at 5%+ yields, market yields remain attractive despite rising Fannie Mae coupon. Developers in Williamsburg/greater Hampton Roads should expect continued institutional competition and limited ground opportunities; focus on value-add conversions or adjacent Tier 2 Virginia submarkets with less competitive ownership density.
